summary: Pend Oreille County summit with a 1929 crow's nest, abandoned in the 1930s; today WillhiteWeb reports only a communication site, on private timber land.

facts.status_note: Crow's nest abandoned in the 1930s. WillhiteWeb reports a small communication site at the summit, not a lookout.
facts.agency: Kaniksu National Forest (firelookout.com); WillhiteWeb says the summit is private timber company land

access.note: WillhiteWeb: private timber company land. No gate signs in 2021, and no issue with walking up the road. Gate signs are not permission from the owner (editor's note).

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists a hiking distance of 1.5 miles and an elevation gain of 1,000 feet.

events.note: Crow's nest, per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb.
WillhiteWeb: the 1941 Metsker map shows nothing at the site.

evidence.supports: summit is private timber company land
evidence.quote: This is private timber company land but in 2021 there were no signs on gates, so no issue with you wandering up the road to the summit.
In 1929 there was a crow's nest. It was abandoned in the 1930s.
Moon Hill Pend Oreille 48.38573 -117.23845 Crowsnest Abandoned
in 2021 there were no signs on gates

evidence.supports: small communication site at the top; highpoint a minute walk from road end
evidence.quote: There is a small communication site at the top and the highpoint is just a minute walk from the end of the road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com names the Kaniksu National Forest. WillhiteWeb describes the summit as private timber company land. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two short pages that agree on the 1929 crow's nest and the 1930s abandonment. No abandonment event is recorded because the sources give only 'the 1930s'. The brief says kind 'platform'; sources say crow's nest. Status 'gone' follows the brief and the WashingtonLookouts index (which marks it Gone); the FFLOS list says Abandoned. Access 'private' is inferred from WillhiteWeb's land note; confirm with the owner before anyone visits. No staff, fires or visit-climbable facts were found. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story no longer calls 1929 the first record (it is the earliest date the two sources give) and drops 'now' from the land-ownership claim.
